title: Remove the remaining exemptions from automatic mutual recognition
action: Phase out the occupations each state has excluded from automatic mutual recognition (for example electricians in WA, and building surveyors and plumbers in Victoria) and the extra conditions placed on interstate workers.
why: Each exemption keeps a barrier to moving interstate for the workers who are often most needed, such as building trades after a disaster or during a housing boom.

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: However, many exemptions and conditions still exist. For example, Western Australia does not currently allow automatic mutual recognition for electricians and Victoria does not currently recognise some occupations, such as building surveyors and plumbers

evidence.source: Housing construction productivity: Can we fix it?
evidence.quote: Whilst automatic mutual recognition has helped improve labour mobility by effectively removing some of the complexities and geographical inconsistencies imposed by occupational licensing systems, not all jurisdictions have signed up. Many exemptions and conditions still exist.
